name: read-swc-where-description-absent
description: The question "which components carry no description?" asked as one filtered read: `where: [{"field": "description", "exists": false}]` over the `swc` layer. `exists` asks whether a VALUE is carried, and a field the element does not carry, a `null` and the empty string `""` are no value. The empty string is the case that matters: every string field of the schema that has a default defaults to `""`, so an element that never wrote a description carries `""` exactly as one that stated `description: ""` does; a clause that matched neither would answer nothing on any real model. The two components without a description are answered — one whose file omits the key and one whose file states it empty — and the base's two described components are not. The `index` form keeps the answer to the identities the question asks for.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose two components (`ExampleSWC`, `ExampleConsumerSWC`) each carry a description, plus two components without one: `UndescribedSWC`, whose file has no `description` key, and `BlankDescriptionSWC`, whose file states `description: ""`.
context.notes: The response carries `""` for both undescribed components in every form that publishes the field, whether the file wrote it or not, and a clause is compared against exactly the value the response would carry — which is why the rule is about the value and not about what the file spelled. `0`, `false` and an empty map `{}` are values: `exists: true` keeps an element carrying one of them.

expected.notes: The identities come in the layer's read order. The negation `exists: true` answers the base's two components and neither of these, so the two clauses partition the layer.
